posts.title: david.reviews: "Everyone in This Bank Is a Thief" by Benjamin Stevenson
posts.description: ★★★★: A delightful continuation of a series that's quickly become a favorite. I appreciate his commitment to fair-play mysteries even if I basically never solve much myself. The clues are there if you're paying attention though! The heist setting was great and there were a lot of layers, per usual. The whole thing is wrapped in a great frame story, too This is maybe my favorite Ernest novel yet! T

posts.title: david.reviews: "The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook" by Matt Dinniman
posts.description: ★★★★: Does a good job smoothing out the detail while focusing on the big picture. I love the media / "the revolution will be televised" angle and the intergalactic worldbuilding. Growing the ensemble is good and some of the more complex plot threads are coming to fruition. Carl is also less terrible at this point, which is probably for the best. posts.title: david.reviews: "Ender's Shadow" by Orson Scott Card
posts.description: ★★★★: Provides a perfect foil to the original novel. I liked Bean as a character explaining so much of his inner monologue and the political machinations around him.
